extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners preparing or prosecuting PCT (international) applications (especially filings via the USPTO electronic filing system)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/formal requirements for preparing the parts of a PCT international patent application (sequence listings, claims, drawings, abstract, fees, priority claims) when filing (particularly via the USPTO). Covers content, format, physical requirements, and procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing — separate part and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Rule 5.2(a), the sequence listing must always be presented as a separate part of the description. When filing an international application (PCT) using the USPTO patent electronic filing system, the sequence listing part of the description may be submitted either as a single ASCII text file with a ".txt" extension or as a PDF file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single ASCII text file will serve both as the sequence listing part of the description under PCT Rule 5.2 and the electronic form under PCT Rule 13ter.1(a) in the absence of a PDF sequence listing file. Submission of the sequence listing in PDF is not recommended because the applicant would also be required to supply an ASCII text copy to the appropriate authority for international search/examination (paragraph 40 of AI Annex C). When both PDF and ASCII are filed and Box IX on the Request does not indicate which forms part of the application, the PDF will be considered to form part of the application and the ASCII will be considered an accompanying item for search purposes under PCT Rule 13ter.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing — size limit for ASCII file via USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: 100 megabytes is the size limit for submitting a sequence listing text file via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure ASCII text sequence listings do not exceed this size when filing through the USPTO system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing — compliance and corrective invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing does not meet the necessary requirements (e.g., submitted in PDF when not appropriate, or the .txt file does not comply with Annex C), the International Searching Authority or the International Preliminary Examining Authority may invite the applicant to furnish, within a fixed time limit, a sequence listing complying with the required standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation may request payment of a late furnishing fee in accordance with PCT Rule 13ter.1(c). Where such an invitation has been issued, the sequence listing and late fee must be submitted to the ISA or IPEA. It is advisable to submit an electronic (text) listing together with the international application rather than wait for an invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing — effect on search/examination without electronic form
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic form (text) is not mandatory in international applications to be searched by the United States ISA or examined by the United States IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if an electronic form (text) of a sequence listing is not provided, a search or examination will be performed only to the extent possible in the absence of the electronic form (text). The U.S. sequence rules (37 CFR 1.821-1.825) and PCT sequence requirements are substantively consistent; full compliance with U.S. rules will generally ensure PCT compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing — effect on international filing sheet count
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence listing filed in an ASCII text file will not be included in the sheet count of the international application (PCT). A sequence listing filed in a PDF file will be included in the sheet count of the international application (PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, an international application filed containing both a PDF file and a text file sequence listing will have its sheet count calculated to include the number of sheets of the PDF sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — general requirements (definition, clarity, support)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought. Claims shall be clear and concise. They shall be fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are set forth in PCT Article 6 and PCT Rule 6 and echoed in 37 CFR 1.436. Claims must define the matter for which protection is sought and be fully supported by the description; the physical requirements for claims are the same as for the description (claims must commence on a new sheet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — number and numbering of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of the claims shall be reasonable in consideration of the nature of the invention claimed. If there are several claims, they shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are amended, the method of numbering is governed by the Administrative Instructions. Where a claim is cancelled, no renumbering of the other claims shall be required; where renumbered, they shall be renumbered consecutively in Arabic numerals. Page/line formatting rules apply (claims should start on a new sheet; page numbers must not be placed in margins; line numbers in right half of left margin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — references to other parts of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not, except where absolutely necessary, rely, in respect of the technical features of the invention, on references to the description or drawings (e.g., 'as described in part...' or 'as illustrated in figure...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the international application contains drawings, the technical features mentioned in the claims shall preferably be followed by the reference signs relating to such features, placed between parentheses. If inclusion of reference signs does not particularly facilitate quicker understanding, they should not be made. Reference signs may be removed by a designated Office for publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — manner of claiming (two-part form and characterizing portion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of the matter for which protection is sought shall be in terms of the technical features of the invention. Whenever appropriate, claims shall contain (i) a statement indicating those technical features necessary for the definition but which, in combination, are part of the prior art; and (ii) a characterizing portion—preceded by words such as 'characterized in that' or equivalent—stating concisely the technical features which, in combination with (i), it is desired to protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims must, whenever appropriate, be in two distinct parts: statement of prior art and the characterizing portion. Where national law of a designated State does not require this manner, failure to use it shall have no effect in that State provided the actual manner used satisfies national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims — form, construction, and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim which includes all the features of one or more other claims (dependent claim) shall do so by a reference, if possible at the beginning, to the other claim(s) and shall then state the additional features claimed. Any multiple dependent claim shall refer to such claims in the alternative only and shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any dependent claim shall be construed as including all limitations contained in the claim to which it refers. All dependent claims referring back to a single previous claim, and all dependent claims referring back to several previous claims, shall be grouped together to the extent and in the most practical way possible. Failure to conform to a particular manner used by an ISA may result in an indication under Article 17(2)(b) in the international search report, but has no effect in a designated State if national law is satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — numbering and identification upon amendment (Administrative Instructions Section 205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the claims under Article 19 or Article 34(2)(b) may be made by cancelling claims, adding new claims, or amending the text. Where a claim is cancelled, no renumbering is required. When renumbered, claims shall be renumbered consecutively in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant shall indicate in the letter referred to in Rule 46.5(b) or Rule 66.8(c) the differences between the claims as filed and as amended, indicating for each claim whether it is unchanged, cancelled, new, replaces one or more claims as filed, is the result of division, replaces previously amended claim(s), or is the result of division of a previously amended claim, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — physical requirements and commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical requirements for the claims are the same as those for the description. The claims must commence on a new sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page/formatting rules include: claims starting a new sheet, page numbers not in margins, line numbers placement (right half of left margin), and other PCT Rule 11 correspondence. Omission of an entire sheet of claims generally cannot be rectified without affecting international filing date except in limited circumstances (see PCT Rules 4.18 and 20.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — when required and what counts as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be required when they are necessary for the understanding of the invention. Flow sheets and diagrams are considered drawings. Where, without being necessary, the nature of the invention admits illustration by drawings, the applicant may include such drawings, and any designated Office may require them to be filed within a prescribed time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are required by a designated Office under Article 7(2)(ii), the time limit shall be reasonable and never shorter than two months from the date of written invitation. Drawings must be presented on separate sheets and may not be included in the description, the claims or the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — size, usable surface, and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of the sheets shall be A4 (29.7 cm x 21 cm). On sheets containing drawings, the usable surface shall not exceed 26.2 cm x 17.0 cm. The sheets shall not contain frames around the usable surface. Minimum margins: top 2.5 cm; left side 2.5 cm; right side 1.5 cm; bottom 1.0 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some receiving Offices may accept other sheet sizes provided the record copy transmitted to the International Bureau is of A4 size. The usable surface and margins must be observed to permit proper reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — permitted text and translation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings shall not contain text matter, except a single word or words when absolutely indispensable (e.g., 'water', 'open', 'closed', 'section on AB'), and in the case of electric circuits and block diagrams, a few short catchwords indispensable for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any words used shall be so placed that, if translated, they may be pasted over without interfering with lines of the drawings. Drawings containing text matter not in a language accepted under PCT Rule 12.1(a) by the International Bureau as a Receiving Office may lead to transmission/processing or denial of international filing date depending on language acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — graphical execution, scale, lettering and proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be executed in durable, black, sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined lines and strokes without colorings. Cross-sections indicated by oblique hatching; scale and distinctness such that a photographic reproduction reduced to two-thirds allows all details to be distinguished; numbers, letters and reference lines shall be simple and clear; height of numbers and letters not less than 0.32 cm; drawing lines ordinarily drawn with drafting instruments; each element in proper proportion to others except where differing proportion is indispensable for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scale is given, it shall be represented graphically. Brackets, circles or inverted commas shall not be used with numbers and letters. Where many reference signs exist, attach a separate sheet listing all reference signs and the features denoted by them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — arrangement, numbering of figures and sheets, and pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The same sheet of drawings may contain several figures. Figures on two or more sheets forming a single complete figure shall be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing parts. Different figures shall be arranged without wasting space, preferably upright; different figures shall be numbered in Arabic numerals consecutively and independently of sheet numbering; figures should be preceded by 'Fig.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sheets of drawings must be numbered in the center of either top or bottom (not in margin) using a separate series (e.g., '2/5'). Where sheets are added, identify by preceding sheet number followed by a slant and Arabic numeral (e.g., 10/1, 15/1, 15/2). Reference signs not mentioned in description shall not appear in drawings, and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — photographs and color
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT makes no provision for photographs but they are allowed by the International Bureau where it is impossible to present in a drawing what is to be shown (e.g., crystalline structures). Where photographs are submitted, they must be on A4 sheets, black and white, respect minimum margins and admit direct reproduction. Color photographs are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings are not acceptable; exceptional photographs must still meet the physical and margin requirements for drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — amendment and rectification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings can be amended during the international phase only if the applicant files a Demand for international preliminary examination and can also be amended during the national phase. The amendment shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure for rectification of obvious mistakes in the drawings is explained in MPEP § 1836. Omission of an entire sheet of drawings cannot be rectified without affecting the international filing date except in limited circumstances (see PCT Rules 4.18 and 20.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — content and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall consist of a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, the claims, and any drawings; it shall indicate the technical field to which the invention pertains and be drafted to allow clear understanding of the technical problem, the gist of the solution, and the principal use or uses of the invention. Where applicable, include the chemical formula which best characterizes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each main technical feature mentioned in the abstract and illustrated by a drawing shall be followed by a reference sign in parentheses. The abstract should be primarily related to what is new in the art to which the invention pertains; it shall be as concise as the disclosure permits (preferably 50 to 150 words in English).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — prohibited content and drafting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application. Phrases implicit (e.g., 'the invention relates to...') and legal phraseology (such as 'said' and 'means') should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract must be drafted as a scanning tool to assist specialists in determining whether to consult the international application itself. Use concise, factual language; avoid superfluous language and prohibited items defined in PCT Rule 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — length, placement and procedural consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferably 50-150 words (if in English or translated into English). The abstract of the international application as filed must begin on a new sheet following the claims and physical requirements correspond to those for the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of an abstract upon filing will not affect the granting of a filing date. However, failure to furnish an abstract within one month from the date of notification by the Receiving Office will result in the international application being declared withdrawn. If the Receiving Office or ISA establishes or modifies the abstract, the applicant may propose modifications or comments until 1 month from the date of mailing of the international search report (PCT Rule 38.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary checklist of abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract preferably 50-150 words and should contain: (A) indication of field of invention; (B) clear indication of the technical problem; (C) summary of invention’s solution of the problem; (D) principal use or uses of the invention; (E) reference numbers of main technical features in parentheses; (F) where applicable, chemical formula which best characterizes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should not contain: (A) superfluous language; (B) legal phraseology such as 'said' and 'means'; (C) statements of alleged merit or speculative application; (D) prohibited items as defined in PCT Rule 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — international filing fee determination for sequence listing files
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculation of the international filing fee for an international application (PCT), including a sequence listing, filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system is determined based on the type of sequence listing file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, ASCII text sequence listings are not included in the sheet count (and thus may affect fee calculation differently), while PDF sequence listings are included in the sheet count; if both are filed, the PDF sheet count is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of international application and related fees (37 CFR 1.446)
rubrics_metrics.description: Money paid for international application fees where paid by actual mistake or in excess may be refunded. Requests for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid (with specific rules for deposit-account charges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions and specifics: international and search fees refunded if no international filing date is accorded or application withdrawn before transmittal of record copy to IB; search fee refunded if withdrawn before transmittal of search copy to ISA; transmittal fee not refunded. Handling fee refunded only in narrow circumstances (e.g., Demand withdrawn before being sent by IPEA). Refund of supplemental search fees made if refund warranted by Director (e.g., successful protest under 37 CFR 1.477). If receiving Office and ISA differ, refund requests after transmission of search copy must be directed to the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim — information to be indicated and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who claims the priority of one or more earlier national, regional or international applications for the same invention must indicate on the Request, at the time of filing, the country in or for which it was filed, the date of filing, and the application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under PCT Rule 4.10, an applicant may claim priority of an application filed in or for a WTO Member even if that State is not party to the Paris Convention. A PCT Contracting State that is not a WTO Member would not be obliged to recognize such priority effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim — correction, addition, and certified copy deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may correct or add a priority claim by a notice submitted to the Receiving Office or the International Bureau within 16 months from the priority date (or within 16 months from the priority date as changed), whichever expires first, provided that a notice correcting or adding a priority claim may, in any event, be submitted until the expiration of 4 months from the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may file the certified copy of the earlier filed national application together with the international application or submit it to the IB or the receiving Office not later than 16 months from the priority date (or earlier if early processing is requested). The IB will normally furnish copies to designated Offices so applicants usually need not submit certified copies to each designated Office.
